overview: This one-page file consists of a 1939 list-of-papers sheet for material concerning sugar-yielding plants and the sugar industry in Formosa (Taiwan). It records a single telegram, no. 82, sent from Taihoku by Emmerson on October 5, reporting the promulgation of an ordinance controlling Taiwan’s sugar industry and enclosing a summary of the Taiwan Government’s regulations; the telegram and enclosure themselves are not present in the supplied text.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Sugar-Yielding Plants in Formosa (Taiwan)
subfiles.about: An index sheet records an October 5 telegram from Emmerson in Taihoku concerning a new ordinance controlling Taiwan’s sugar industry.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists one item under the subject of sugar-yielding plants in Formosa (Taiwan). Telegram no. 82, sent from Taihoku by Emmerson on October 5, announced the promulgation of an ordinance intended to control the island’s sugar industry. According to the entry, it enclosed a summary of the relevant Taiwan Government regulations, but neither the telegram nor its enclosure appears in the supplied file text.

interest: The sheet is useful as evidence that the U.S. State Department monitored Japanese colonial regulation of Taiwan’s strategically important sugar industry immediately before the Second World War. Although the substantive telegram and enclosure are absent, the index preserves their date, origin, sender, subject, and reported enclosure, providing a lead for locating the missing documents elsewhere in the archival series.
